newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Police raid Belgian diamond trade HQ, arrests made.
newsitem.headline: Police raid Belgian diamond trade HQ, arrests made.

text.p: Police searched the headquarters of the Belgian diamond trade in the port city of Antwerp on Thursday in connection with the bankruptcy of a bank, and arrested one employee, the prosecutor's office said.
Police have been investigating the bankruptcy in January of Antwerp Bank Max Fischer.
"(The search) is a consequence of the bankruptcy," Antwerp public prosecutor's office spokeswoman Leen Nuyts told Reuters.
She said a controller of the Antwerp Diamond Office, which handles formalities of diamond imports and exports, was arrested on charges of forgery, bribery and complicity in money laundering.
The Diamond Office is part of the Diamond High Council (DHC), which represents and promotes the diamond business in Antwerp.
Three other people, all working for the same diamond company, were arrested on Wednesday on charges of forgery, fiscal fraud and money laundering, Nuyts said.
"The investigation (into the bank) showed that more companies used fictitious accounts or unlawful practices," Nuyts said.

Earlier this month, police arrested three men from the Antwerp diamond scene in connection with the Fischer bank bankruptcy on charges of having laundered an estimated $28 million, fraud, tax evasion and culpable bankruptcy.

Bank Max Fischer's licence was revoked in January by Belgium's regulatory Banking and Finance Commission as a result of what it called "serious irregularities (which) threatened the good outcome of commitments (of the bank)".
The Antwerp diamond sector has annual turnover of 600 billion francs ($16.8 million) and employs 30,000. ($ = 35.7 Belgian francs)
